rationale: The literature indicates that variants in PLAA, originally described as causing a postnatal progressive neurodegenerative syndrome (neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies; NDMSBA), can indeed be identified prenatally in fetuses displaying structural ultrasound abnormalities. Specifically, prenatal whole-exome sequencing of deceased fetuses presenting with fetal ultrasound structural anomalies identified pathogenic/likely pathogenic compound heterozygous variants in PLAA (Huang et al., 2023). Furthermore, clinical curation panels such as Genomics England PanelApp classify PLAA under panels assessing severe microcephaly, ataxia, and cerebellar anomalies manifesting with prenatal presentations.

evidence.text: In a cohort of deceased fetuses with ultrasound abnormalities evaluated by whole-exome sequencing, compound heterozygous variants in PLAA were identified in association with neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies (NDMSBA), confirming fetal structural presentations.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact correlation between the degree of residual PLAA functional activity (nullizygous vs. hypomorphic missense variants) and the timing of onset of detectable cerebellar hypoplasia or microcephaly (prenatal second trimester vs. early postnatal)?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether complete loss-of-function null alleles consistently lead to prenatal structural cerebellar hypoplasia/ventriculomegaly while hypomorphic missense alleles present primarily with postnatally acquired microcephaly will inform prenatal genetic counseling and variant interpretation.
